<meta>continues from previous page; running header: 論語註疏大全 (Complete Commentaries on the Analects); page number 二五 (25)</meta>to sum up a whole person in a single word, or a whole era in a single deed, is in every case wrong.

Feng Houzhai <note>Feng Yi, a Song-dynasty scholar styled Houzhai</note> said: If we judge him by his drafting of the three codes of punishment and his casting of the penal statutes in bronze <note>Zichan of Zheng had the laws of punishment cast on bronze vessels in 536 BCE, a move criticized by the statesman Shuxiang</note>, then what he fell short in was truly a great deal. From the words of the <term>Chunqiu</term> <gloss>Spring and Autumn Annals</gloss> we know that his share of the Way of the gentleman was truly slight. <note>The OCR reading of this sentence may be corrupt; the sense is that Zichan only partly embodied the gentleman's Way.</note> The sage's words neither inflate praise beyond the merit nor inflate blame beyond the fault. On the phrase "he employed the people with righteousness," the Collected Commentary alone traces what actually happened, and that reality cannot be hidden. <note>The wording of this sentence in the OCR is unusual and may be garbled.</note>

○ Master Hu said: The mourning of three years; Confucius; "the sons and younger brothers whom he taught": a love bequeathed to posterity. "The fields that he made fruitful": and when he died, "the sons and younger brothers whom he taught": a love bequeathed to posterity. <note>This passage appears garbled in the OCR. It echoes the song of the people of Zheng recorded in the Zuo Commentary, "Our sons and younger brothers, Zichan taught them; our fields, Zichan made them fruitful," and Confucius's lament at Zichan's death, calling him "a love bequeathed from antiquity."</note> Zichan's whole spirit lay in the single word "righteousness" <note>original: "義"</note>. As for the people's saying that he was "kind but did not understand governing" <note>a judgment of Mencius, who criticized Zichan for ferrying people across rivers in his own carriage instead of building bridges</note>, that refers only to the single matter of helping people across, nothing more.

○ The Master said: "Yan Pingzhong was good at keeping company with others. Even after long acquaintance, he still treated them with respect."

Yan Pingzhong was a grandee of Qi; his personal name was Ying. Master Cheng said: When people keep company for a long time, respect fades. To be able, after a long time, still

<summary>This page closes the Ming compilers' discussion of Confucius's assessment of Zichan of Zheng, arguing that the sage's praise was exact and that Zichan's character centered on righteousness. It then opens the Analects passage praising Yan Pingzhong of Qi for keeping respect toward friends over long acquaintance, with the commentary of Cheng Yi.</summary>
<keywords>Analects, Zichan, Zheng, Yan Pingzhong, Yan Ying, Qi, Confucius, Cheng Yi, Feng Houzhai, Master Hu, penal code, righteousness, kindness, respect, friendship, Sishu daquan, Hu Guang, Neo-Confucian commentary</keywords>
